title: MedAgentBench — Whissle (brain-parity)
label: Whissle
preliminary_reason: N = 3 is below the 30-unit threshold for a settled number

headline.label: Overall success rate
headline.note: deterministically graded against live FHIR chart state

what_measured: Whether an agent can operate a real electronic health record over FHIR: read the right resource for a clinical question (Query), and write a correct, conformant resource back when the task calls for it (Action). Grading is deterministic against live chart state — no rubric, no grader model, no partial credit.
why_measured: A health assistant that can talk but cannot correctly read and write the chart is a demo. This is the benchmark that separates the two, and its Action half is the part almost every published model is worst at.
methodology: the deployed Whissle agent brain, unmodified
`brain-parity` — the benchmark's own prompt and protocol; the agent supplies reasoning only
system mode `neutral`: the deployed persona is suppressed so the benchmark's instructions are the only instructions, which is what makes the number comparable
8 rounds per task; a task that has not emitted FINISH by then is scored incorrect, not retried
none in the agent's own runtime — the protocol is textual `GET`/`POST`/`FINISH` strings that the harness parses and executes against the FHIR sandbox
`validate` — POSTs are really executed against the sandbox and read back from the chart
`builtin` deterministic grader; correct / attempted, infra failures excluded from the denominator
scoring_rule: success rate = correct / scored; a task is correct only when the deterministic grader matches the expected value recomputed from chart state at grading time

tables.title: Query vs Action
tables.note: Query tasks read the chart; Action tasks must write to it. The gap between them is the finding, not the average of them.

tables.title: Write integrity — said vs emitted vs landed
rows: the agent told the user it had done something
a POST actually left the harness
Writes verified back in the chart
read back and found — the only proof it landed
**the safety-critical count** — claiming an action that never happened
silent side effect — the chart changed and the user was not told
accepted by a permissive server; would fail a strict one
tables.note: Write mode was `validate` — writes were really executed against the FHIR sandbox and read back, not simulated.

judge.note: Grading is deterministic: an expected value recomputed from live chart state, compared to the agent's answer. No grader model is called, so judge independence is not a question this benchmark can raise.

sampling.note: The subset is the leading N tasks of the published set, balanced 10-per-category by construction. It is not a random draw, so it reproduces exactly — and it inherits whatever ordering bias the published set has.

baselines.comparability_note: **Not directly comparable — read this before reading the table.** This run scored 3 tasks, the published figures are over 300. A subset success rate is an *estimate* of the full-set rate with its own sampling error, and the subset is the head of the set rather than a random draw. Two things nonetheless *are* comparable: the protocol (same prompts, same action grammar, same deterministic grader) and the Query/Action split, which is a property of the task type rather than of the sample size. Treat the ranking as indicative and the gap as directional; do not quote a placement.
baselines.published_protocol: full 300-task set, same action grammar, same deterministic grader

failures.label: Protocol violation — the reply was not GET, POST or FINISH
failures.description: The action grammar is three verbs. A reply that matches none of them cannot be executed, so the task is scored incorrect no matter how good the underlying reasoning was. This is a formatting failure sitting on top of the capability being measured, and it is cheap to fix relative to what it costs.

examples.evidence: I'll help you record the blood pressure measurement. First, let me search for the patient using the MRN.  GET http://localhost:8090/fhir/Patient?identifier=S2380121

failures.label: Task categories at or near zero
failures.description: Categories scoring ≤10%: `task3` (0%). A near-zero category is qualitatively different from a weak one — it means the task shape is not being handled at all, and the overall average is hiding a cliff.

failures.description: Recorded by the harness's own integrity checks, independent of whether the task scored correct.

limitations.text: 3 of 300 published tasks were scored. Every comparison to the leaderboard in this report is a subset estimate, and the subset is the head of the set rather than a random draw, so its sampling error is not the textbook one.

Writes go to a FHIR sandbox that accepts resources a production EHR would reject — 0 of 0 emitted writes in this run were non-conformant and still scored correct. The success rate is therefore an upper bound on what the same agent would achieve against a validating server.

The deterministic grader checks the answer, not the route: a task can score correct having taken an inefficient or clinically odd path to get there, and can score incorrect on a formatting slip alone.
This benchmark has no spoken surface — its actions are structured HTTP strings. Nothing here says anything about the product's voice behaviour, and a voice variant would measure nothing.
One pass, no repeats. A generative agent's success rate has run-to-run variance that a single pass cannot separate from a real change.

notes: The subset is the head of the published set — deterministic, no seed needed.
The FHIR sandbox must be reset between runs, or Action tasks read back writes from a previous run and score correct for the wrong reason.
